headline_findings: Tauri 2.11.5 + wry 0.56 is current (Sept 2026); use >=2.11.1 to avoid CVE-2026-42184 origin confusion on Windows.
Sidecar + shell-plugin arg allowlist is the sanctioned llama-server pattern: spawn from Rust, stream tokens over Channel.
Token deltas are tiny so plain Channel (fast eval path under 8 KB JSON) beats exotic binary IPC; images go via custom protocol, never invoke.
WebView2 Evergreen is preinstalled on Win11; downloadBootstrapper default keeps installer lean, offlineInstaller adds ~127 MB.
Updater minisign signing is mandatory and fits Cerebro's single opt-in network touch; MSI=WiX Windows-only, NSIS is cross-compilable.

items.fit_reference_machine: Excellent: zero extra runtime on Win11; offline-first preserved. Evergreen auto-patches Chromium without bundling ~180 MB.
items.harness_integration: Pin tauri >=2.11.1, wry 0.56, bundler 2.9.x; use downloadBootstrapper + minimumWebview2Version; keep fixedVersion out.
items.name: Tauri 2.11.5 core + wry 0.56 / WebView2 Evergreen
items.quality_cost: None; newer WebView2 fixes rendering/security bugs. Fixed-version pinning would freeze bugs in.
items.reported_gain: No tok/s gain (GUI shell). wry 0.56.1 fixes a Windows WebView2 parent-subclass crash; 2.11.4 fixes HDC leak hurting resize.
items.what: Current Tauri v2 stack (core 2.11.5, wry 0.56, tao 0.35/0.36) rendering via OS Evergreen WebView2/Chromium on Windows.
items.where_implemented: tauri 2.11.5, tauri-bundler 2.9.4, wry 0.56.0, webview2-com 0.38.x via Evergreen runtime

items.fit_reference_machine: Excellent: pure config, no runtime cost. Deny-by-default matches extreme-security goal and offline posture.
items.harness_integration: Ship one capability per window (chat, settings, admin); never windows:[*]; CI-grep for *:default grants and remote urls entries.
items.name: Capabilities ACL (allow/deny, per-window, remote)
items.quality_cost: None on output; misconfig breaks features loudly (permission-denied) rather than silently.
items.reported_gain: No throughput gain; shrinks blast radius of XSS to only granted commands. Remote origins ACL-enforced since Apr 2026.
items.what: JSON/TOML capabilities granting named plugin permissions to specific windows/webviews/platforms; unmatched webviews get zero IPC.
items.where_implemented: src-tauri/capabilities/*.json + app.security.capabilities in tauri.conf.json (Tauri v2 ACL)

items.fit_reference_machine: Good: AES-GCM per-message overhead negligible on i9-12900H, but adds latency to every token event if applied to chat window.
items.harness_integration: Optional: apply isolation only to untrusted-preview window (RAG HTML), keep chat on brownfield + tight capabilities.
items.name: Isolation pattern (sandboxed IPC interceptor)
items.quality_cost: None if hook is pass-through; buggy hook can corrupt IPC args.
items.reported_gain: Security only; adds small per-message AES-GCM cost. Recommended by Tauri except for perf-sensitive paths.
items.what: Sandboxed JS app that intercepts, validates, and AES-GCM-encrypts every frontend IPC message with per-run keys.

items.fit_reference_machine: Excellent: build-time only. Matches offline posture; no CDN scripts allowed anyway.
items.harness_integration: Set restrictive CSP (self + ipc: + asset:), keep dangerousDisableAssetCspModification false, freezePrototype true, withGlobalTauri false.
items.name: CSP nonces/hashes + freezePrototype + asset scope
items.quality_cost: Over-strict CSP breaks fonts/images until allowlisted; freezePrototype can break libs mutating Object.prototype.
items.reported_gain: No speed gain; blocks XSS payload and prototype-pollution IPC hijack. Asset scope deny overrides allow.
items.what: Build-time CSP nonce/hash injection, Object.prototype freezing, and glob-scoped asset: protocol gating convertFileSrc loads.
items.where_implemented: app.security.{csp, assetProtocol, freezePrototype, dangerousDisableAssetCspModification} in tauri.conf.json

items.fit_reference_machine: Perfect fit: updater is the only sanctioned network path, matching opt-in update check; artifacts reuse the MSI/NSIS installer.
items.harness_integration: Gate updater:default capability behind opt-in toggle; static latest.json over HTTPS; guard TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY in CI; never lose key.
items.name: Updater plugin with mandatory minisign signatures
items.quality_cost: None on model quality; wrong latest.json/signature bricks updates until fixed.
items.reported_gain: No tok/s gain; mandatory Ed25519 verify before install. TLS enforced; v1Compatible zip mode kept for v1 migrants, removed in v3.
items.what: In-app updates (check/download/install + relaunch) with mandatory Ed25519 signature verification against embedded pubkey.

items.fit_reference_machine: Perfect fit: llama-server/whisper.cpp ship as versioned sidecars beside the 8 GB-VRAM-aware backend picker; batch-1 unaffected.
items.harness_integration: externalBin llama-server-<triple>.exe; spawn from Rust with argv allowlist; stream SSE via Channel; kill on RunEvent::Exit; one persistent server.
items.name: Sidecar processes via shell plugin (externalBin)
items.quality_cost: None; stale sidecar binary ships stale backend unless versioned with harness.
items.reported_gain: No tok/s gain; avoids per-inference respawn (spawn ~50-200 ms + multi-second model reload on this laptop).
items.what: Bundled child binaries spawned with argv only (no shell); execute vs spawn gated by shell:allow-execute/spawn with exact arg allowlists.

items.fit_reference_machine: Ideal for token streaming on this laptop: per-token deltas (~10-50 B) stay on the fast eval path; batch only if deltas exceed 8 KB.
items.harness_integration: Stream tokens over Channel<string>; batch tool-call JSON; use emit_raw only for ArrayBuffer payloads; never push images via eval.
items.name: IPC Channel streaming (eval/fast vs fetch/slow path)
items.quality_cost: None; chunking too coarse adds UI latency, too fine adds bridge overhead (~300 us floor for small payloads).
items.reported_gain: Payloads <8192 B JSON / <1024 B raw use direct eval (~2x faster than fetch on WebView2 v135); larger use fetch-pull. 150 MB resp 29s->23s after #10641.
items.what: Streaming IPC primitive: small messages delivered by direct JS eval, large ones staged server-side and pulled with fetch.

items.fit_reference_machine: Good for thumbnails/plots on the laptop; keeps JS main thread free. Token path unaffected.
items.harness_integration: Serve images/audio via custom scheme or asset: scope; signal readiness over Channel; frontend fetch()es bytes natively.
items.name: Custom-protocol byte serving (invoke bypass)
items.quality_cost: None; adds protocol-registration code and CSP/scope entries to audit.
items.reported_gain: Community image bench: Vec<u8> over invoke arrives as JSON number array (worst); custom scheme fetched natively is fastest, ~zero main-thread cost.
items.what: Serving binary blobs over a custom URI scheme / asset protocol fetched by the frontend instead of base64/JSON-array over invoke.
items.where_implemented: register_uri_scheme_protocol / with_asynchronous_custom_protocol (wry, always-on since 0.56) + asset: scope

items.fit_reference_machine: Good: downloadBootstrapper keeps offline installer lean; Win11 needs no runtime fetch. offlineInstaller (+127 MB) only for air-gapped offices.
items.harness_integration: Default downloadBootstrapper + minimumWebview2Version gate; offer offlineInstaller build flavor for air-gapped small offices.
items.name: WebView2 install modes + minimumWebview2Version
items.quality_cost: fixedVersion freezes Chromium bugs; skip breaks the app if runtime missing.
items.reported_gain: Size deltas: embedBootstrapper +1.8 MB, offlineInstaller +127 MB, fixedVersion +180 MB; downloadBootstrapper +0 MB.
items.what: Five installer strategies for the WebView2 runtime plus a minimum-version gate that triggers the bootstrapper.

items.fit_reference_machine: Good: isolate untrusted RAG previews/cookies per profile on shared runtime; negligible memory cost for 2-3 profiles.
items.harness_integration: Use default profile for chat; named profiles for plugin/untrusted preview webviews; deny device permissions by default handler.
items.name: wry 0.56 permission handler + WebView2 named profiles
items.quality_cost: None; over-denying breaks getUserMedia/geolocation features until allowed.
items.reported_gain: Security/isolation only; covers all 12 COREWEBVIEW2_PERMISSION_KIND values with Allow/Deny/Prompt.
items.what: Unified per-request permission API across backends plus isolated cookies/storage/IndexedDB per named WebView2 profile.

items.fit_reference_machine: Good: NSIS per-user install needs no admin on office machines; MSI suits managed per-machine deploy. Both reuse updater artifacts.
items.harness_integration: Ship NSIS per-user default + MSI per-machine; custom .nsi hooks only if needed; sign via signCommand; watch 7-call HSM cost.
items.name: MSI (WiX v3) vs NSIS installers + signing
items.reported_gain: No tok/s gain; NSIS cross-compiles via cargo-xwin, MSI needs Windows + VBSCRIPT feature. Signing now covers WiX/NSIS DLLs (7 calls).
items.quality_cost: None on model quality; unsigned inner DLLs may trip strict AVs; post-build signing needs Store-zip + BOM-free JSON care.
items.what: WiX MSI (Windows-only build, needs VBSCRIPT feature) vs NSIS setup.exe (cross-compilable, hooks, per-user/per-machine) with Authenticode signing.

items.what: Official create-tauri-app SolidJS/TS template plus community starters (router, Tailwind, window-controls) on Vite.
